subject: 🏃 Saturday — Rest / Travel Home (Wk 9)
html:
Tomorrow: Rest day. Fly home to Redwood City. No workout. A 20–30 min easy jog is optional if time allows before the flight, but pure rest is the better call — you’ve had a solid Week 9 so far (threshold reps Wednesday, easy run Thursday, BW strength today), and Sunday’s 16-miler with 8 @ MP is the week’s centerpiece. Bank the recovery.

Sunday preview — the session that matters: 16 mi long run, first 8 easy by HR (140–155), last 8 @ marathon pace by HR (150–160; ~7:35–7:45 readout). Hilly home route. Priority #1: take at least 2 gels during the MP block at HR 150–160. This is the remaining validation before the Jul 12 dress rehearsal — proving the fueling system works at effort, not just at easy pace (the Presidio lesson). Fueling plan: Maurten DM 160 in handheld (40 g) + gels every ~25 min (Gel 100 or CAF 100), with 2× CAF in the back half → targeting 70–80 g/hr. You proved 71 g/hr GI-clean on Jun 29 at easy effort; now prove it at MP.

Focus cue: Hydrate well on the flight home — cabin air + travel dehydration going into a 16-miler is the sneaky risk. Drink steadily through the afternoon/evening. Also: confirm the H10 chest strap is home and charged — Sunday’s MP block needs reliable HR data (you ran BC without it).

Context: Week 9, Phase 3 — Peak Volume & Power. 22 days to the SF Marathon. This is the biggest-volume week of the build (~44 mi), and Sunday’s 16 with 8 @ MP is the key quality session. You’re coming in with a clean knee (1/5 all week), a solid threshold hit Wednesday, and a fueling system that worked at 71 g/hr on Jun 29. Tomorrow is about arriving home rested, hydrated, and ready to execute Sunday morning.

Prep tonight: Pack the H10 strap in your carry-on (not checked bag). Lay out Sunday’s fueling kit before bed — DM 160 packet, 4–5 Maurten gels (at least 2 CAF 100), LMNT, handheld bottle. Set an alarm that gives you time to eat oatmeal + banana 60–90 min before stepping out the door.
